Styles and Form Factors of Hearing Instruments

Hearing aids come in several physical styles depending on your hearing loss severity, cosmetic preference, ear canal anatomy, and manual dexterity.

BTE (Behind-The-Ear)

The electronics sit in a casing comfortably behind the ear, connected to an acoustic tube and custom earmould. Best for severe to profound losses and young children.

RIC (Receiver-In-Canal)

The world’s most popular style. The speaker sits directly inside the ear canal connected by an ultra-thin wire. Barely noticeable and provides very natural sound quality.

ITE (In-The-Ear)

Custom made to fit in the outer ear bowl. Easy to handle with larger controls and longer battery life for elderly patients.

CIC & IIC (Invisible-In-Canal)

Fits deep into the ear canal. Virtually invisible from the outside for maximum cosmetic discretion.

Pediatric Hearing Care: Nurturing Speech & Language

Hearing is the biological cornerstone of spoken language, social learning, and intellectual development. A child learns speech by listening to their parents and surroundings from the earliest months of infancy.

Why Early Pediatric Intervention Matters

If hearing loss is left undiagnosed in infants, speech milestones are severely delayed. With early diagnosis via newborn OAE/BERA screening and timely fitting of pediatric hearing devices (such as Phonak Sky), children can learn, attend mainstream schools, and communicate with complete confidence.

Key Features of Pediatric Hearing Aids

  • Tamperproof Battery Drawers: Prevents curious infants and toddlers from opening the battery compartment.
  • Robust Water & Dust Resistance: Rated IP68 to withstand play, sweat, and unpredictable outdoor conditions.
  • Visual Indicator Lights: Reassures parents and teachers that the device is powered and functioning.
  • Roger Wireless FM Compatibility: Direct streaming from the classroom teacher’s wireless microphone straight to the child’s hearing aids.

How Do Modern Digital Hearing Aids Work?

Unlike old analog amplifiers that simply made all sound louder (including painful background traffic and fan noise), modern digital hearing aids function like high-speed miniature computers inside your ear.

The 4-Stage Acoustic Process

  1. Microphone Pickup: Directional dual microphones capture acoustic sound waves from your surrounding environment and convert them into electrical signals.
  2. Digital Signal Processing (DSP): The central processor analyzes sound hundreds of times per second. It separates human speech from background noise, suppresses wind turbulence, and amplifies only the specific frequencies where you have hearing deficits.
  3. Receiver / Speaker Delivery: The refined digital signal is converted back into acoustic sound waves and delivered precisely into the ear canal.
  4. Acoustic Neural Transmission: Your auditory nerve receives clear sound vibrations and transmits them to the brain for natural cognitive comprehension.

Modern Hearing Aids for a Modern World

A hearing aid is a sophisticated miniature medical electronic device designed to amplify sound frequencies selectively so that individuals with sensorineural or conductive hearing loss can listen, communicate, and participate fully in daily life.

Guidance by Patient Experience

I have not worn hearing aids before

On average, people wait 7 to 10 years after experiencing hearing difficulties before seeking help. During this time, the brain’s auditory cortex loses familiarity with high-frequency speech consonants. Modern digital devices are lightweight, automatic, and ease you gently into hearing clearly again.

I have worn hearing aids before

If your devices are more than 3-5 years old, modern platforms feature artificial intelligence noise cancellation, direct smartphone Bluetooth audio streaming, rechargeable lithium-ion batteries, and effortless speech tracking in crowded Bangladeshi gatherings.

Abid Hearing Care Centre provides a complete spectrum of audiological diagnostic evaluations and technical maintenance services performed with calibrated, state-of-the-art medical instruments.

1. Diagnostic Hearing Evaluations

We perform comprehensive tests to determine the exact type, degree, and configuration of hearing impairment:

  • Pure Tone Audiometry (PTA): Air and bone conduction testing to evaluate hearing thresholds across standard speech and high frequencies.
  • Auditory Brainstem Response (ABR / BERA): Measures electrical brain activity in response to sound; vital for infants and neuro-audiological diagnosis.
  • Auditory Steady-State Response (ASSR): Provides frequency-specific threshold estimates for infants and severe hearing impairments.
  • Otoacoustic Emissions (OAE): Tests cochlear outer hair cell function for rapid newborn hearing screening.
  • Impedance Audiometry & Tympanometry: Evaluates middle ear function, eardrum mobility, and Eustachian tube dysfunction.

2. Digital Hearing Aid Selection & Computerized Fitting

Using digital manufacturer fitting software, our audiologists calibrate hearing devices specifically to match your prescription curve. We ensure optimal speech clarity while protecting residual hearing against loud sounds.

3. Custom Ear Mould & Acoustic Shell Laboratory

In-house laboratory producing medical-grade ear moulds customized to the unique ear canal anatomy of every patient:

  • Soft silicone moulds for pediatric comfort and feedback-free high-power amplification.
  • Hard acrylic moulds for durability and easy insertion for adult patients.
  • Custom micro-shells for invisible Completely-in-the-Canal (CIC) and In-the-Canal (ITC) instruments.

4. Maintenance, Repair & Sonic Cleaning

Complete servicing center equipped to repair and maintain all major hearing aid models:

  • Speaker/Receiver replacement & sound distortion correction.
  • Microphone mesh unclogging and transducer replacement.
  • Ultrasonic moisture extraction and wax barrier clearing.
  • Battery door replacement and contacts cleaning.

About Abid Hearing Care Centre (AHCC)

Founded in 2014 by Mohammad Haidar Ali (Audiologist with Clinical Competence in Audiology), Abid Hearing Care Centre has grown to become Dhaka’s premier clinical audiology clinic dedicated to patient-centered, ethical hearing rehabilitation.

Our Mission & Clinical Philosophy

Hearing loss is not simply a volume problem — it affects brain cognitive health, emotional connection, and quality of life. At AHCC, our philosophy is anchored on three clinical pillars:

  • Precision Diagnosis Before Device: We never sell hearing devices over the counter. Every client undergoes rigorous audiometric evaluation in an ISO-calibrated soundproof booth.
  • Certified Technology: As an authorized partner of Swiss Sonova (Phonak) and leading German/Danish brands, we guarantee 100% genuine hardware with international warranty support.
  • Continuous Rehabilitation: Hearing adaptation takes time. We provide free follow-up fine-tuning sessions, regular cleaning, and auditory counselling for the lifetime of your device.

Clinic Organization & Team

Our multidisciplinary team comprises 9 full-time audiology and technical specialists and 12 support staff operating across clinical audiology, acoustic ear-mould fabrication, and specialized device servicing.

Hearing means quality of life. Make better living.

The ability to hear is such a fundamental part of life that most people take it for granted. Hearing is essential for everyday communication. It connects us with family, friends and co-workers.

  • ✓Conversations with family and friends
  • ✓Meetings, calls and work
  • ✓TV, music and the sounds you love
👂

We rarely think about the role our ears play in our lives, until something changes.

10 years

the average time people wait before doing something about their hearing loss.

Don't wait too long

On average, people with hearing loss wait almost 10 years before they act. Only a few make a timely decision to recover their hearing and improve their quality of life.

Understanding hearing loss

Hearing loss usually begins unnoticed. Even simple conversations can become tiring, and many parts of everyday life get harder. Hearing loss can have many causes, but in most cases it can be addressed successfully.

Conversations with loved ones
Harder to follow, more tiring.
Meetings and phone calls
Missed words and repeated questions.
Watching TV
Turning the volume up and still missing speech.
Social life
Many people withdraw and become isolated, and quality of life drops.

There's nothing like the sound of Paradise

People expect great sound quality, multifunctionality and control from a hearing aid. Phonak Audéo™ Paradise delivers sound quality, universal connectivity and personalised digital solutions.
